title: Level 2 (Intermediate) - D-11
notes:
West leads the ♥A against 4♠. West's ♥A wins the first trick and West continues hearts for South to ruff. There may be a trump loser if that suit breaks 4-2, but there is probably only 1 club loser as West's opening bid makes him a big favorite to hold the ♣A.

It would be a mistake for South to draw 3 rounds of trump immediately. East's discard on the third round of spades is a serious problem. South will eventually have to play on clubs to set up a trick with the ♣K, but West will take his ♣A and draw South's last trump. The defense will now be free to run the heart suit.

South can guard against this danger by playing a club toward dummy's ♣K before drawing trump. West will take his ♣A, but West's heart return (no defense is better) can be ruffed in the dummy. It is now safe to draw 3 rounds of trump. South then reverts to diamonds and West is welcome to ruff whenever he wants. South's remaining trump can handle West's heart return, leaving South with the balance of the tricks.
